blocking_facts.no_gate_no_consumer: ci-lint gate IS the CI-OK aggregator. A repo without one has nowhere to consume a reuse decision; only 2 of 34 have it.
blocking_facts.economics_flip: Measured on clud: a main-push run is 14.9 runner-min, 7.1 (48%) skippable. At 1.63 pushes/day reuse saves ~5 runner-min/day, while a nightly minimal-tier run costs 14.9/day and a full-tier one ~60/day. The design's drift backstop costs 3-12x what it protects at clud's real push rate (the design assumed ~30 pushes/day). Prefer --max-age-hours over a nightly until a repo's push rate justifies one.

A 0% verdict is a statement about the probe until the exact display names have been checked.

measured_eligibility.finding: The ROI is concentrated, and concentrated harder than #318 recorded. Five repositories carry essentially all of the measurable saving: clud, kernal-api and template-python-rust-cmd are adopted; soldr and zccache are promotable on measurement but blocked on wiring, not on economics. The long tail of 29 is each worth well under a runner-minute a day or has no eligible merges at all, so adopting it would add review surface and skip-guarding risk for noise. Two independent probe defects had written off the second-largest prize (soldr) as a non-adopter; see probe_failure_modes. Re-measure rather than adopt blindly.
measured_eligibility.note_on_cache: Per owner directive 2026-10-04: a daily catch-all run is fine for cache revalidation but is superseded by cache promotion (setup-soldr `auto`, nearest-ancestor restore, CACHE-024). Where a repository already has a scheduled full matrix (running-process, template-python-rust-cmd) or enough naturally-must-run pushes to refresh on their own (kernal-api, ~1 full run per 6 days at 89.5% reuse), no nightly is added. setup-soldr's `auto` key covers the build-cache family today; it does not yet cover `dylint`.

probe_failure_modes.duplicate_display_name: soldr's ci.yml has two jobs whose display name is both `Lint` (lint-docs, a deliberate no-op for docs-only and attested heads, and lint, the real one). reuse-check requires every job carrying a required name to conclude success, so the sibling that skips by design failed the check and reported `required-job-not-success`. Fixed in ci.yml#320, which now reports `ambiguous-required-job` naming the offending job ids and conclusions. That single ambiguity is what produced the false 'soldr never reuses' conclusion.
probe_failure_modes.name_matches_nothing: A --required-job that matches no job at all makes every run decode as `required-job-missing`, which reads identically to a repository that never reuses. This produced the second false reading, on the dominant job name. A 0% reuse verdict should be treated as a probe bug until the exact display name has been checked against `gh run view <id> --json jobs` on a run that did succeed.
probe_failure_modes.consequence_for_measurement: Two independent probe defects both pointed at 'soldr is not a reuse candidate'. With the ambiguous name removed it measures 75% reusable (#320, required job `Lint` removed) and 65% on its dominant job (this measurement, `Linux x64 / x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`). Both agree soldr is a high-value adopter and neither matches the recorded 0.0%.
probe_failure_modes.reproduce: GH_TOKEN=<token> python3 -m ci_lint reuse-report --repo <owner/name> --workflow ci.yml --required-job '<exact, unambiguous plan-derived job display name>' --since 2026-09-20 --limit 20

cache_writer_skips_are_not_savings.rule: Name the skip target by whether the job WRITES a cache, not by how long it takes. In zccache every setup-soldr job (fmt, dylint, msrv, docs, miss-overhead) is a main-push cache writer behind `save-cache-remote`, so the most expensive job, Dylint at 5.9 of 20.0 runner-min, must keep running: skipping it freezes the dylint cache family and is the CACHE-022 shape (`ci.yml#153`).
cache_writer_skips_are_not_savings.correction: This supersedes the first zccache reading in ci.yml#321, which quoted Dylint 6.0 min as the dominant skippable job and ~5.5 runner-min/day. Both were arithmetically correct and operationally wrong: Dylint is a writer, so those minutes are not recoverable by reuse.
cache_writer_skips_are_not_savings.measured_per_job_zccache: Mean successful main-push cost, 8 runs: Dylint 5.9, Reflink e2e 3.5, Cache pre-prune barrier 2.8, Miss overhead budget 2.5, MSRV 2.1, Formatting 1.7, Documentation 1.4, CI mode 0.2; total 20.0 runner-min per push.
cache_writer_skips_are_not_savings.actual_saving: Reflink e2e is the only pure-validation job with meaningful cost -- it calls no setup-soldr and writes nothing. 3.5 min at a 0.90 reuse rate and 10.4 pushes/day is ~3.3 runner-min/day, against ~5.5 claimed on the Dylint reading. Still the best-measured repository in the fleet, but a third of what #321 claimed.
cache_writer_skips_are_not_savings.cost_of_being_wrong: Adopting on the Dylint reading would have produced a green main branch whose dylint caches silently stopped refreshing -- the exact failure the whole mechanism exists to make impossible, introduced by the adoption itself.

cache_promotion_gap.setup-soldr-auto-is-build-cache-only: Per setup-soldr's own README, the `key: auto` nearest-ancestor pilot is a 'Build-cache override only' -- 'Other families keep their identity keys.' So dylint-output-cache (and every other family) gets no ancestor promotion.
cache_promotion_gap.why_it_matters: zccache's dominant main-push job is Dylint (~6.0 runner-min, 29% of a 21.0 min push). Its dylint-output-cache is saved on success but only ever restored under its own identity key, so the nearest-ancestor win that makes the build cache cheap is unavailable to the job that costs the most.
cache_promotion_gap.candidate: Extend `auto` from build-cache-only to the whole family, or at minimum to dylint-output-cache. Owner directive 2026-10-04: 'caches from the family should be promoted when possible.'
